stages.request: Chained conversions drift because `convert()` rounds what it returns: converting `1 in` to `km` and that result back to `in` gives `0.984252 in`. `convert()` should return the exact converted value and no longer accept `precision` or `rounding`. `format_quantity()` should take those two keyword arguments instead, with the same defaults, so a value is rounded only when it is turned into text.

`unitconv convert '3 Mm' km` prints `0.000003 km`: the megametres are read as millimetres, and `5 MN` comes out as millinewtons. Unit symbols should be case-sensitive, matched exactly as written. A symbol that matches a unit only when case is ignored should be refused with a hint listing the spellings it could mean, for example `unknown unit: 'MM' (did you mean 'Mm' or 'mm'?)` or `unknown unit: 'KM' (did you mean 'km'?)`.

Scripts reading `unitconv convert ... --json` need the unit's name as well as its symbol. In that JSON object, `unit` should become an object with `symbol` and `name`, for example `"unit": {"symbol": "km", "name": "kilometre"}`. The name is always singular, whatever `--style` says, and compound units get their spoken name, such as `kilometre per hour`.

`unitconv list` prints all 38 units at once and scrolls off the screen. Show a page at a time: a `--per-page N` option, default `20`, and a `--page N` option, default `1`, with a last line such as `page 1 of 2`. A page number below 1 or past the last page should exit with status 2 and print `error: page 3 out of range (1-2)` to standard error.
Compound units in results are hard to read, as in `1 kg*m^2/s^2`. Write them with a middle dot between units and superscript powers instead, as in `1 kg·m²/s²` and `9.81 m/s²`.

`unitconv convert '0.235 m' cm --precision 0` prints `23 cm`, although 23.5 rounds to 24 under the default `half_even` mode, and `unitconv convert '0.145 m' cm --precision 0 --rounding half_up` prints `14 cm` instead of `15 cm`. The conversion produces 23.499999999999996 before any rounding happens. Conversions should use decimal arithmetic instead of float, so that values round the way they are written.
